statement: A rhombus has perimeter $52$, and one of its diagonals has length $24$. What is the area of the rhombus?

choices.misconception: I multiplied the side, 13, by the other diagonal, 10, as if that diagonal were the height of the rhombus.
I used the side, 13, in place of the other diagonal and computed (1/2)(24)(13) = 156.
I multiplied the two diagonals, 24 and 10, and forgot the one half.
I multiplied the given diagonal by the side, 24 times 13 = 312.

hints: Each side is $52 / 4 = 13$. The diagonals of a rhombus cut each other in half at right angles.
The diagonals split the rhombus into four congruent right triangles, each with hypotenuse $13$ and one leg $12$.
The other leg is $5$, so the second diagonal is $10$. The area of a rhombus is half the product of its diagonals.

solutions.reliable: Each side has length $52 / 4 = 13$. The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so half of the given diagonal, $12$, and half of the other diagonal form the legs of a right triangle with hypotenuse $13$. That is a $5$-$12$-$13$ triangle, so the other half-diagonal is $5$ and the other diagonal is $10$. The area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 24 \cdot 10 = 120$.
solutions.elegant: The diagonals cut the rhombus into four right triangles with legs $12$ and $5$. Each has area $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 12 \cdot 5 = 30$, so the rhombus has area $4 \cdot 30 = 120$.
